final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mainly narrowed the claim to a conditional, caveated position based on the same record. That clarification is analytically useful but it does not resolve the core compliance gap. Under the stated policy, certification may proceed only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and the material segment weakness is disclosed or covered by an approved mitigation. The present record still lacks the current model-card or packet language and lacks approved mitigation or reviewed risk acceptance. Aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents support launch readiness, but they are not sufficient to satisfy the unresolved documentation predicate. This is why the case remains suspicious rather than compliant_with_caveats: caveated compliance would require evidence that the caveat has actually been implemented in the certification packet, whereas here the caveat is itself the missing compliance condition.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the current release model card or certification packet actually discloses the health-plan benefits regression as a material limitation.
No approved mitigation or reviewed risk-acceptance record is in evidence for the affected segment weakness.
The missing current disclosure is a policy predicate for certification, not a minor caveat that can be assumed satisfied from argument alone.
Prior approval from nine weeks ago and informal monitoring comments remain contextual only and cannot satisfy the current-release evidence requirement.
